title: Mis rated hard
statement: Find the number of subsets of $\{1, 2, \dots, 16\}$ containing no two elements that differ by $3$ or by $5$, modulo $1000$.
hints: Encode a subset as a binary string.
Scan left to right, remembering the last five positions.
solution: Scan the numbers from $1$ to $16$ in order, remembering which of the last five were chosen. A transfer over these $32$ states gives $1324$ subsets, which is $324$ modulo $1000$. Why this works. recursion: a scan with a short memory turns the count into a transfer between states.
